subject: POC capacity planning — Acme AI trial (reserved GPUs & autoscale)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@acme.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC capacity planning - follow up and next steps

Hi Samir / Alexis -

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment heading into the trial: 

POC goals / success criteria:
- Evaluate response latency at 99th percentile under production-like query mix (target <= 350ms).
- Validate end-to-end correctness on 3 representative prompts (accuracy/regression vs your baseline).
- Measure cost per 1M tokens and projection for production scales.

Evaluation plan / ownership:
- Acme: provide 2 canonical datasets (intent + long-form context) and the expected pass/fail criteria by EOD Wed (Alexis).
- Redwood (Marissa + Solutions): run trials, capture token-level metrics, and share dashboard.
- Infra owner: Rishi to provision reserved capacity and set autoscale policies.

Capacity ask (what we need from infra/ops):
- Reserved baseline: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs for the two-week trial window (Sept 7-20) to guarantee predictable latency for initial evaluation.
- Autoscale headroom: allow burst up to 8 GPUs for short spikes (expected burst length 10-20 minutes).
- Target sustained throughput: ~75 QPS (average), peak burst up to ~300 QPS. Typical tokens per request: 350-800 tokens.
- Monitoring: 1-minute metrics and a shared Slack channel for alerts during the trial.

Timeline / next steps:
1) Acme to confirm datasets and success criteria by Wed, Sept 2.
2) I'll send an SOW for signature today (DocuSign link below).
3) Rishi - can you confirm capacity reservation and autoscale plan by EOD Thurs, Sept 3?
4) Kickoff call with infra + Acme on Mon, Sept 7 to flip traffic to reserved pool.

Attachments: Acme_POC_capacity_plan_v1.pdf (attached) - includes traffic profile and cost estimate.

Thanks - happy to jump on another call if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0134

Redwood Inference - Production-first inference runtime

From: Samir Patel <samir@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alexis Gomez <alexis@acme.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC capacity planning - follow up and next steps

Thanks Marissa - this looks good and aligned with our expectations. A few clarifications from our side:

- Datasets: Alexis will upload the two datasets to the shared Drive by EOD Wed (Sept 2).
- Traffic profile: we'll aim to simulate production by replaying 48 hours of traffic. Expected average QPS ~60-90, peak bursts up to ~320 QPS for short windows.
- Tokens: we typically see ~600 tokens/request on average, some up to ~2k for long-form generation.
- Burst behavior: bursts can last up to 30 minutes during specific cron-driven jobs; we can flag those windows in the traffic replay.
- Monitoring: yes to a Slack channel (we prefer a dedicated channel and 1-minute metric granularity).

One ask: can Redwood enable an autoscale policy that allows a short warm-up to avoid cold-start latency when spinning GPUs? Even 60-90 seconds of more aggressive scaling would be helpful. Also please include an estimate for incremental cost if we hit the full 8-GPU burst for 30 minutes.

We'll review the SOW once it's in DocuSign. Looking forward to the kickoff.

- Samir
Samir Patel
Head of ML Infrastructure, Acme AI
samir@acme.ai | +1 (650) 555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@acme.ai>, Alexis Gomez <alexis@acme.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 12:22:00 -0700
Subject: ACTION: Reserve GPUs + autoscale for Acme AI POC (Sept 7-20)

Rishi / Infra team -

Please see the thread above and the attached capacity plan. Ask is to provision the following for the Acme AI POC window: 

- Reserve 4x A100-equivalent GPU baseline from 2026-09-07 00:00 UTC through 2026-09-20 23:59 UTC.
- Autoscale cap: up to 8 GPUs for burst traffic. Policy should allow aggressive scale-up with graceful scale-down; prefer a short warm-up cadence (60-90s) for new instances to reduce cold-starts.
- Network/storage: ensure KV cache persistence across restarts for the trial (we rely on prefix caching for cost/latency).
- Observability: enable 1m metrics retention and open a dedicated Slack channel (#poc-acme-ai).

Attachments: Acme_POC_capacity_plan_v1.pdf (drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cAcmePOC)
DocuSign SOW: https://www.docusign.com/ACME-POC-SOW-12345

Can you confirm capacity reservation, expected incremental cost for a full 8-GPU 30-minute burst, and any constraints we should flag to the customer? Ideally we have a confirmation by EOD Thurs, Sept 3 so we can send the signed SOW and lock the window.

Thanks -
Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir@acme.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACTION: Reserve GPUs + autoscale for Acme AI POC (Sept 7-20)

Looping in infra ops - we can cover this. Quick confirmations and notes:

- Reserved capacity: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved for the Sept 7-20 window. I'll create the reservation and send the allocation ID once provisioned.
- Autoscale: cap configured at 8 GPUs. We'll use a warm-up policy that spins up additional nodes conservatively but accepts the 60-90s warm-up request; note there will be a brief latency bump while KV caches populate.
- Burst cost: incremental estimate for 8 GPUs for 30 minutes is ~USD $420 (ballpark, depends on spot vs reserved pricing); I'll provide a firm quote after the reservation is created.

- Observability: enabling 1m metrics and will create the Slack channel #poc-acme-ai and invite both Acme and our oncall.
- KV cache: we will try to persist the cache across node swaps, but if we hit full scale-up there's a short period where cache misses may increase latency. Recommend flagging long bursts (>=20 minutes) during the replay so we can soak the cache ahead of critical windows.

I'll follow up with the allocation ID and confirmed cost by Wed EOD. If you want, we can run a warm-up run on Sept 6 to pre-populate caches.

- Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
